Click Start to generate an HTML version.
Download the resulting .html file — images are embedded, so it's a single file.

items.q: Is converting PDF to HTML free?
items.a: Yes, converting PDF to HTML is free within the daily usage limits shown above.

items.q: Will the HTML look pixel-for-pixel identical to the PDF?
items.a: No. This preserves the document's reading order, text, and images, not an exact visual layout — a PDF's precise positioning doesn't translate into simple, editable HTML. For PDFs made mostly of body text and images, the result is very close; for complex multi-column or design-heavy PDFs, expect a simplified, linear version.

items.q: What happens to images in the PDF?
items.a: Images are embedded directly inside the HTML file (as data URIs), so the download is a single file with no separate image files to keep track of.

items.q: Will my file be kept private?
items.a: Yes. Files are processed securely and automatically deleted after a short retention period.
